Snyk.author: dns_snek
Snyk.text: > I don’t dispute capitalismBut we should. This is a taboo topic but pretending that these consequences are either disconnected from capitalism or that capitalism is some natural law of the universe that should never be challenged is, for lack of a better word, delusional.These consequences are inherent to capitalism because people benefiting from it demand infinite growth and nobody is incentivized to care about the environment. People who care about it get outcompeted by those who don't in ruthless pursuit of "efficiency".We can try to regulate it to the point that people wouldn't call it capitalism anymore but the nature of a system where the only incentive is maximizing profit will always have a natural tendency to harm the environment, so it should be disputed.

Snyk.author: lwansbrough
Snyk.title: Show HN: Per Diem, a daily dice game like Balatro
Snyk.text: I love Balatro and have had a fascination with daily games recently. RNGdle in particular sparked my interest because of its dopamine-factory style gameplay. Per Diem takes a similar approach.In Per Diem, each day you cast 5 dice from a sack randomly. The pips and patterns (ie. snake eyes) are scored, producing your final score for the day. You get one roll a day, so the challenge is maximizing your scoring potential. Charms are the mechanism by which you tilt the odds in your favour: charms can modify the pip score and the multiplier. Each day presents a new "encounter" which slightly modifies the rules of the game, requiring a new strategic approach.Because charms are not freely available, the game scales over days as you score points, earn coins, and purchase better charms from the shop. In order to keep your score and charms you should sign in. Currently only Discord sign ins are supported - this is admittedly a bit of a growth hack: when you sign in, you can see a leaderboard for each Discord server you're apart of, which makes competition a little more fun.I made this mostly as a fun way to test out my knowledge on how to build a viral product with some built in growth mechanisms, and now I'm testing to see if it holds up against an audience like HN. :) Let me know what you think!

CodeQL.author: pat-s
CodeQL.text: (founder of codefloe)We have a custom integration for "Pages" in partnership with statichost.eu. You'll get a fully provisioned static website (h3 enabled) in < 1m with the click of a button. Custom domains are supported. Effectively the same what GH Pages offer :)See https://docs.codefloe.com/pages/

CodeQL.author: pat-s
CodeQL.text: (founder of codefloe)Codeberg is buckling because of old hardware and not-so-great operational devops processes. I am stating that as a former core member with access to these and the historic goals of changing something to the better. The underlying software is not the issue.GitHub and GitLab were built on Ruby. The language behind this is much less suited to serve a platform with that many requests.The hard part is the SRE engineering behind it and the option to potentially make tweaks in the underlying codebase when needed, to fix possible bottlenecks (most often it comes down to how SQL is being processed).

CodeQL.author: pat-s
CodeQL.text: (founder of codefloe)Numbers are just one thing, what counts is the effective request traffic. We are just as large as we are and can't do anything about it ;)The only thing we can influence is to stay fast from day to day, watch our disk and storage and adjust things if needed.I am quite confident that we can take multiple tens of thousands, if not hundred of thousands of users (with the respective request ratio share of active and dead accounts) with our current hardware stack. We'll see how it goes when we eventually get there.

CodeQL.author: pat-s
CodeQL.text: (founder of codefloe)Repo data, which is the majority of the data, is stored on disk. "Packages" (including container images) and other image data on S3. Not on AWS, so costs are like 1/5 or less. We have per account quotas for different types of storage.All of this is transparently explained in our docs. No need for speculation ;)
